requirement_text.REQ-428: Third MOB-4 requirement. Task routes (lib/letflow/routers/tasks.ex): GET /api/v1/tasks/inbox, GET /api/v1/tasks/:id, POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/claim, POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/complete. The task form is resolved through REQ-424's pinned resolver and rendered by REQ-427's form renderer; never the active version. Process-instance renderer: read-only view of GET /api/v1/instances/:id and /api/v1/instances/:id/timeline (lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex) -- status, current step, timeline. No cancel/rebind/advance actions (not in MOB-4). All screens use REQ-426's six-state wrapper; claim/complete errors (409 already claimed, 403, 422) map to its states.

task.description: Hard gate per WF-02 Step 3b. Apply the ISS-0880 lesson: for every multi-clause acceptance criterion (AC1 has 4 clauses: list/claim/open/complete-with-body; AC4 has 3: status/timeline/no-cancel-rebind-advance), confirm EACH clause individually has a runnable test that would fail specifically if that clause were violated -- not a single test asserting the AC's gestalt. Read test/specs/REQ-428.md and the actual test files independently (not TEST-DESIGNER's handoff summary). Check: (a) every AC clause has >=1 targeted test, no TODO/skip without a passing counterpart, (b) test fixtures use per-test unique data, no cross-test pollution, (c) tests are self-sufficient (don't depend on run order), (d) no hardcoded secrets/connection strings, (e) the AC4c 'no cancel/rebind/advance' guard is a genuine structural guard (e.g. grep/import-absence check), not just an absent assertion. FAIL immediately on any check failure, naming the specific gap.
acceptance_criteria: Every clause of AC1 (list/claim/open/complete) has its own targeted test
Every clause of AC4 (status/timeline/no-action) has its own targeted test, with the no-action clause being a structural guard not an absence of assertion
AC2 (pinned version resolution) and AC3 (409 conflict + inbox refresh) each have a dedicated test
No test fixture pollution, no hardcoded secrets, tests self-sufficient
